legend: Anup was working tirelessly to finalize the problem set for the upcoming Insomnia contest. Meanwhile, Darsh, having absolutely nothing better to do, wandered over to demand a treat(chapo in local lingo). Hoping to get back to work, Anup struck a deal: Darsh would get his chapo, but only if he could first solve a seemingly innocent, yet "not-so-simple" problem.
Anup describes a process to build a tree:

Given an integer n$$$n$$$, construct an array a[a1,a2,…,an]$$$a[a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n]$$$ of size n$$$n$$$ consisting of zeroes and ones where a1=0$$$a_1= 0 $$$. Consider a tree with n+1$$$n+1$$$ vertices labeled 0,1,2,…,n$$$0, 1, 2, \ldots, n$$$, where vertex 0$$$0$$$ is designated as the root.
ai=0$$$a_i = 0$$$, add an edge between vertex i$$$i$$$ and vertex i−1$$$i-1$$$;
ai=1$$$a_i = 1$$$, add an edge between vertex i$$$i$$$ and vertex i−2$$$i-2$$$.

Let h(a)$$$h(a)$$$ be the height of the tree for one possible valid array a$$$a$$$. Anup asks Darsh to find the sum of h(a)$$$h(a)$$$ over all possible valid arrays of 0$$$0$$$s and 1$$$1$$$s where a1=0$$$a_1 = 0$$$. Since this sum can be incredibly large, output the answer modulo 109+7$$$10^9 + 7$$$.
input: The first line contains a single integer t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤104$$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases.
The only line of each test case contains a single integer n$$$n$$$ (1≤n≤2⋅105$$$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the size of the array.
output: For each test case, output a single integer — the sum of the heights of the trees formed by all valid arrays, modulo 109+7$$$10^9 + 7$$$.
